question: Every year between January and May, along the southern coasts of Italy, many tens of tons of young sardines (Sardina pilchardus) are fished illegally. The undersized fish are illegally sold in markets, often in broad daylight. The Adorno Group, O.D.V.

, specialising in anti-poaching, sent as many as 16 reports to the competent authorities in 2023 alone, regarding both the illegal fishing of young sardines and the equally illegal marketing of undersized specimens of Swordfish (Xiphias gladius), accompanied by photographic evidence. All the reports have remained unanswered and have not produced any outcomes, while illegal sales have continued.

Sea controls on the fishing of young sardines are very scarce, not least because they have sometimes provoked violent reactions from illegal fishers. In fact, the actions of the Italian law enforcement agencies to counter these illegal phenomena focus almost exclusively on the transportation phase, by which time the fish are dead and serious environmental damage has been done.

Does the Commission intend to take action against the Italian Government, calling for systematic controls, both at sea and on land, aimed at ensuring compliance with national and European regulations established to protect marine fauna and biodiversity?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.

2024) On the basis of Regulation (EC) No 1224/20091 (the Control Regulation), Member States are responsible for controlling fishing activities carried out in their waters, as well as for taking the appropriate measures of follow-up in the event of infringements of the rules of the common fisheries policy (CFP) committed by natural or legal persons, including professional or recreational fishers.

The EU applies a zero tolerance approach to illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, as reflected in the practice and policy agenda of the Union, as well as in the changes recently brought to the Control Regulation by Regulation (EU) 2023/28422.

Among those changes, particularly relevant are those related to serious infringements for the marketing of products stemming from IUU fishing committed by natural or legal persons. The Commission was not informed of the reports and photographic evidence mentioned by the Honourable Members and would welcome receiving them.
If they so warrant, the Commission will engage with the Italian authorities to clarify the issue and exchange about the necessary measures, in line with Title XI of the Control Regulation.

Besides, the Commission is confident that the full and timely implementation by the Member States of the recently adopted revision of the Control Regulation will reinforce control and compliance with the rules of the CFP across the EU, including in Italy.
